trust_decision.summary: Keys from a caller-supplied schema (propertyDependencies name/value) and from instance data must not resolve to or write through Object.prototype; decided when propertyDependencies is parsed into a two-level map and looked up during validate/reduce.

landing_point.why: The advisory summary names parsePropertyDependencies in propertyDependencies.ts.

fix_sites.module_kind: shared merge utility; fix.diff:85-86 change is NOT present at pinned (reverted)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: mergeSchema2 only does single-level assignment into a fresh object, so a __proto__ key swaps that local object's prototype rather than polluting Object.prototype; and the maintainer reverted the Object.create(null) change there, which suggests it broke things.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Merged schemas from mergeSchema2 must stay ordinary objects; the upstream Object.create(null) change to mergeSchema2 was reverted (pinned code keeps {}), so a blanket null-prototype hardening of merge output likely breaks callers that rely on Object prototype methods.

O6_input_shapes: __proto__ as propertyDependencies property name (two-level write into Object.prototype)
instance value coerced via template string and looked up with hasProperty (non-string values, inherited names like constructor/__proto__)

O7_producer.where: src/keywords/propertyDependencies.ts:76-125 (parse builds node[KEYWORD] consumed by findMatchingSchemata at :18-39)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: dependentSchemas reducer looks up instance keys with dependentSchemas[propertyName] == null, so inherited names (constructor, toString) resolve to prototype members
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Different keyword; impact is lookup confusion on a local map, not global prototype pollution

O8_uncovered_routes.route: dependentSchemas validator plain bracket lookup on instance keys
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: isSchemaNode/boolean checks downstream filter most inherited values
